title: On‑Prem optimizer: safe apply/rollback + offline policy enforcement for batching & caching
creator: Jonas Patel
description: Add a hardened safe-apply flow for batching/caching recommendations targeting Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. Must support offline dry-run verification, strong policy enforcement (OPA/Gatekeeper-style), and an auditable, atomic rollback mechanism that works in air-gapped environments and with KMS-backed key management. Goal: reduce token cost by recommending safe batching/caching deltas while guaranteeing latency SLOs and compliance constraints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CLI/console 'dry-apply' produces a detailed delta report (resource changes, expected cost delta, latency risk score) without changing runtime state in on‑prem clusters.
2) Policy engine blocks any suggested change that would violate organizational policies (max batch size, P95 latency tail increase > X%, disallowed quantization levels).
3) Rollback creates and restores an immutable snapshot of runtime config within 60s for typical cluster sizes; rollback works without internet access in air-gapped mode.
4) End-to-end integration tests run in CI that simulate offline dry-run and an approved apply; tests validate observability hooks (Grafana dashboard shows expected cost drop, no SLO violation).
5) Audit logs written to customer-managed storage and surfaced in Console with links to PRs and dry-run reports.
implementation_notes: Design a two-phase apply: (a) dry-apply -> deterministic simulator that replays sampled traffic against new batching/caching configuration, (b) gated apply -> dry-apply artifacts + signed approval triggers agent to commit changes.
For Private/on‑prem: package simulator as a binary container so it can run in air-gapped environments; use local traffic dump as input. Avoid dependence on external qps APIs.

Use OPA policies authored by security/compliance to evaluate deltas. Provide a small builtin policy set and allow upload of org policies to the private control plane. Decision: prefer OPA Rego for flexibility and match with existing infra knowledge.

State snapshot/rollback: persist config snapshots to the customer-controlled object store (S3-compatible) or local filesystem with HMAC-signed manifests. Store checksum and apply sequence ID in Console audit event.
Fallback semantics: when an apply fails post-commit, automatically trigger rollback and create an incident ticket. Provide manual override for emergency rollbacks (requires 2 approvers).

Latency safety checks: conservative default limits for batching and cache TTL in Private by default (safe-defaults). System exposes an explicit knob 'aggressive_optimizations' that is disabled by default in Private mode.
testing_plan: Create synthetic traffic generator (rw-sim) to produce representative request distributions and KV cache hit patterns for dry-run simulator.
Unit tests for policy evaluation logic using Rego scenarios (include deny/allow edge cases).
Integration test: run dry-apply -> signed-approve -> gated-apply in a forked VPC cluster CI job; validate metrics via Grafana compare panel.
Air-gapped smoke test: run the entire flow in an on-prem test lab without internet; confirm snapshots are stored locally and rollback succeeds.
Chaos test: inject latency spikes during apply to validate automatic rollback triggers and alerting.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only in 'onprem-lab' cluster; manual review and postmortem after each apply (1 week).
Canary: enable for 5 customers on dedicated capacity with explicit opt-in and 24/7 on-call coverage (2 weeks).
GA: enabled as opt-out for dedicated/Private customers after approval; safe-defaults remain enabled unless org toggles 'aggressive_optimizations'.
notes: Tradeoffs discussed with PM (Marta Ruiz) on 2025-02-14: tighter safe-defaults reduce immediate cost savings but dramatically lower customer risk and support burden.
Security raised need for HSM/KMS compatibility; we will gate certain snapshot encryption flows behind customer-managed KMS integration. (PR: #1012)
We considered using an internal 'simulated load' service but rejected due to network egress concerns in air-gapped installs; local containerized simulator chosen instead.
Estimate increased after spike analysis: clusters with >500 pods require incremental snapshot chunking to meet rollback SLA.
